producer_report.summary: `athena check --history` now takes `[history] exempt` from the tip's config, so an entry added after the commit it names takes effect. I added a new `exempt` field to `HistoryState` in `invariant.rs`. `check_history` fills it from `tip_config`, and `invariant::check` uses it when history state is present. Without history state (per-commit checks) it still uses the parent's list. If the tip's config doesn't parse, the built-in list applies, because `tip_config` already falls back to the built-in config. Validation is unchanged: full ids only, and a new entry must name a commit already in history. The comment above the exemption check and the doc comment on `HistoryState` both say the list comes from the tip and why. I added two tests in `history.rs`. One shows a hand-change commit exempted by a later intervention commit gives no violations at the tip. The other shows a commit made after the entry is still flagged, and an entry naming a commit not in history is flagged as a Configuration violation. I added decision D61 to `docs/decisions.md`, updated the `docs/enforcement.md` map row (D61 and the two test names), and added a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. All checks pass. The two `lib.rs` and `content.rs` files in the deliverable list needed no changes.

checks_run.note: 48 athena-gate tests pass, including the two new ones and the existing exemption tests. The workspace policy test that checks every test named in the enforcement map exists also passes.

open_issues: I did not add a test for the unparseable-tip case, which uses the built-in exempt list.
`HistoryState::default()` has an empty exempt list. Any caller that builds a `HistoryState` without filling it would exempt nothing; the only such caller today is `check_history`, which fills it.
The deliverable list named `lib.rs` and `content.rs`, but neither needed changes.
mistakes: I tried a grep through Bash, which the policy denied, and switched to the Grep tool.
learnings: Violation.commit holds the first 12 characters of the commit id.
`docs/enforcement.md` names tests in a map that `tests/policy.rs` checks against the code, so any new test cited there must exist.
`config_at` failing falls back to `builtin_config()` in `check_history`, which is why the unparseable-tip case needs no extra code.
